patch_excerpts.patch:
--- a/agent/extensions/dynaflows/engine/guardrails/commands/init/harness.py
+++ b/agent/extensions/dynaflows/engine/guardrails/commands/init/harness.py
@@ -5,5 +5,4 @@ from pathlib import Path
 PACKAGE = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[2]
 AGENT = PACKAGE.parents[3]
-SKILLS = AGENT / "skills"
 RECORDS = AGENT.parent / "repos"

new file mode 100644
--- /dev/null
+++ b/agent/extensions/dynaflows/EXTERNAL-DEPENDENCIES.md
@@ -0,0 +1,134 @@
+# External dependencies
+
+What dynaflows relies on outside `agent/extensions/dynaflows`. Backticked paths are repo-relative
+unless they start with `~` or `<`; `tests/dynaflows-extension.test.ts` checks they exist.
+
+## Harness and omp runtime
+
+| Dependency | Location | What it does for the extension |
+| --- | --- | --- |
+| Extension load | `agent/config.yml` | `extensions:` entry loads `index.ts`, `skills/`, `rules/` |
+| Worktree base | `agent/config.yml` | `worktree.base`; guard requires worktrees under it |
+| Judge role | `agent/config.yml` | Model behind `judge()` for structure and advisories |
+| omp extension API | `package.json` | `@oh-my-pi/pi-coding-agent` 19.0.0: `z`, events, `exec` |
+| omp settings registry | `package.json` | `lookup("ttsr.disabledRules")`; mode toggles rules |
+| omp tools | omp core | `bash`, `edit`, `ast_edit`, `read`, `xd://`, `skill://` shapes |
+| omp eval kernel | omp core | Runs `workflows.py`; gives `agent`, `wait`, `judge` |
+| Bun runtime | omp core | `Bun.YAML` reads `rails.yml`; `Bun.Glob` matches globs |
+| Folder rules | `agent/extensions/AGENTS.md` | No `node_modules` imports; zod from omp |
+| Health marker | `agent/extensions/extension-health.ts` | Expects dynaflows to register |
+| Config root | Repo root | Records, scripts, `dynaflows.json` resolve by position |
+| `AGENT` env var | omp runtime | Stripped from every repo command |
+| `OMP_WORKTREE_DIR` | omp runtime | Overrides `worktree.base` in the guard |
+
+## Repo config and build
+
+| Dependency | Location | What it does for the extension |
+| --- | --- | --- |
+| Python project | `pyproject.toml` | Editable engine; ruff, mypy, coverage scope |
+| Python lock | `uv.lock` | Locks the editable engine for `uv run --locked` |
+| Python version | `.python-version` | Interpreter for the engine and its tests |
+| JS lock | `bun.lock` | Frozen JS deps, including omp types |
+| TypeScript | `tsconfig.json` | Strict type check of extension TS |
+| Bun config | `bunfig.toml` | Test root `tests/` |
+| Lint config | `.oxlintrc.json` | Complexity limits, anti-slop rules |
+| Anti-slop plugin | `tools/oxlint/anti-slop` | Custom oxlint rules for extension TS |
+| Markdown lint | `.markdownlint-cli2.jsonc` | 160-column limit for `skills/**` |
+| Prettier | `.prettierrc.json` | Engine rule YAML parsed as JSON |
+| Git allowlist | `.gitignore` | Tracks

+from __future__ import annotations
+
+import re
+
+STRING = r"""(?:"(?:[^"\\\n]|\\.)*"|'(?:[^'\\\n]|\\.)*'|`[^`\n]*`)"""
+DOTTED = r"[A-Za-z_$][\w$]*(?:\.[A-Za-z_$][\w$]*)+"
+ENVIRONMENT = r"process\.env|Bun\.env|import\.meta\.env"
+BINDINGS = {
+    "python": re.compile(
+        rf"^[ \t]*([A-Za-z_]\w*)[ \t]*(?::[^=\n]+)?=[ \t]*({STRING}|{DOTTED})[ \t]*$",
+        re.MULTILINE,
+    ),
+    "typescript": re.compile(
+        rf"\b(?:const|let|var)[ \t]+([A-Za-z_$][\w$]*)[ \t]*(?::[^=\n]+)?=[ \t]*"
+        rf"({STRING}|{DOTTED})(?=[ \t]*(?:;|$))",
+        re.MULTILINE,
+    ),
+    "go": re.compile(
+        rf"^[ \t]*(?:const[ \t]+|var[ \t]+)?([A-Za-z_]\w*)[ \t]*(?:[A-Za-z_][\w.]*[ \t]*)?"
+        rf"(?::=|=)[ \t]*({STRING})[ \t]*$",
+        re.MULTILINE,
+    ),
+}
+DESTRUCTURED = re.compile(
+    rf"\b(?:const|let|var)[ \t]*\{{([^}}]*)\}}[ \t]*=[ \t]*({ENVIRONMENT})\b"
+)
+PROPERTY = re.compile(r"^\s*([A-Za-z_$][\w$]*)\s*(?::\s*([A-Za-z_$][\w$]*))?\s*$")
+WRITE = re.compile(r"[ \t]*(?:[-+*/%|&^]?=(?!=)|:(?!:))")
+
+
+def destructured(source: str) -> tuple[dict[str, str], list[tuple[int, int]]]:
+    bound: dict[str, str] = {}
+    spans = []
+    for match in DESTRUCTURED.finditer(source):
+        spans.append(match.span())
+        for item in match[1].split(","):
+            named = PROPERTY.match(item)
+            if named:
+                bound[named[2] or named[1]] = f"{match[2]}.{named[1]}"
+    return bound, spans
+
+
+def bindings(
+    source: str, language: str
+) -> tuple[dict[str, str], list[tuple[int, int]]]:
+    bound, spans = destructured(source) if language == "typescript" else ({}, [])
+    for match in BINDINGS[language].finditer(source):
+        bound[match[1]] = match[2]
+        spans.append(match.span(1))
+    return bound, spans
+
+
+def inline_bindings(source: str, language: str) -> str:
+    bound, spans = bindings(source, language)
+    if not bound:
+        return source
+    names = "|".join(sorted(map(re.escape, bound), key=len, reverse=True))
+    pattern = re.compile(rf"(?<![\w$.])({names})(?![\w$])")
+
+    def substitute(match: re.Match[str]) -> str:
+        start = match.start()
+        defining = any(low <= start < high for low, high in spans)
+        if defining or WRITE.match(source, match.end()):
+            return match[0]
+        return bound[match[1]]
+
+

+

+guard or handling path. The guidance above stays the policy; the rubric applies it the same way each time.

+| Criterion              | Pass evidence                                                           | Fail                                            |

+| Observable outcome     | A caller-visible result, error, side effect or stored state differs     | Only internals, wiring, logs or prose change    |

+from __future__ import annotations
+
+import hashlib
+from collections.abc import Mapping
+from dataclasses import dataclass
+
+from guardrails.adapters.go.source import (
+    TEST_NAME,
+    has_errors,
+    parse,
+    test_functions,
+    words,
+)
+
+SUFFIXES = (".go",)
+
+
+class CollectionError(ValueError):
+    pass
+
+
+@dataclass(frozen=True)
+class Case:
+    selector: str
+    fingerprint: str
+
+
+@dataclass(frozen=True)
+class Collected:
+    cases: tuple[Case, ...]
+    behaviours: Mapping[str, str | None]
+
+
+def behaviour(name: str) -> str:
+    match = TEST_NAME.match(name)
+    prefix = match.group(1) if match else ""
+    return " ".join(words(name[len(prefix) :]))
+
+
+def fingerprint(body: str) -> str:
+    return hashlib.sha256(" ".join(body.split()).encode("utf-8")).hexdigest()
+
+
+def collect(path: str, text: str) -> Collected:
+    root = parse(text)
+    if has_errors(root):
+        raise CollectionError(f"{path} does not parse as Go")
+    cases = []
+    behaviours: dict[str, str | None] = {}
+    for function in test_functions(root):
+        name_node = function.field("name")
+        body = function.field("body")
+        if name_node is None or body is None:
+            continue
+        selector = f"{path}::{name_node.text()}"
+        if selector in behaviours:
+            raise CollectionError(f"duplicate test function: {selector}")
+        behaviours[selector] = behaviour(name_node.text())
+        cases.append(Case(selector, fingerprint(body.text())))
+    return Collected(tuple(cases), behaviours)

+from __future__ import annotations
+
+import hashlib
+from collections.abc import Mapping
+from dataclasses import dataclass
+
+from guardrails.adapters.go.source import (
+    TEST_NAME,
+    has_errors,
+    parse,
+    test_functions,
+    words,
+)
+
+SUFFIXES = (".go",)
+
+
+class CollectionError(ValueError):
+    pass
+
+
+@dataclass(frozen=True)
+class Case:
+    selector: str
+    fingerprint: str
+
+
+@dataclass(frozen=True)
+class Collected:
+    cases: tuple[Case, ...]
+    behaviours: Mapping[str, str | None]
+
+
+def behaviour(name: str) -> str:
+    match = TEST_NAME.match(name)
+    prefix = match.group(1) if match else ""
+    return " ".join(words(name[len(prefix) :]))
+
+
+def fingerprint(body: str) -> str:
+    return hashlib.sha256(" ".join(body.split()).encode("utf-8")).hexdigest()
+
+
+def collect(path: str, text: str) -> Collected:
+    root = parse(text)
+    if has_errors(root):
+        raise CollectionError(f"{path} does not parse as Go")
+    cases = []
+    behaviours: dict[str, str | None] = {}
+    for function in test_functions(root):
+        name_node = function.field("name")
+        body = function.field("body")
+        if name_node is None or body is None:
+            continue
+        selector = f"{path}::{name_node.text()}"
+        if selector in behaviours:
+            raise CollectionError(f"duplicate test function: {selector}")
+        behaviours[selector] = behaviour(name_node.text())
+        cases.append(Case(selector, fingerprint(body.text())))
+    return Collected(tuple(cases), behaviours)

+  (``tiers``).

+  (``dialect``). ``report-check --dialect bun_test --exit-code <bun's exit code>`` then reads the
+  report; the exit code is required.
+- ``guard-evidence REPORT --tier T``: the report's journal shows the tier's guards were armed.
+- ``affected --base REF [--head REF]``: the selector and T2 files this adapter runs.

+"""The Bun adapter: evidence for the shared test checkers from Bun's built-in ``bun test``.
+
+``guardrails adapter bun_test <action>`` when the profile's ``adapters`` include ``bun_test``:
+
+- ``lint [PATH ...]`` (default): source rules for ``bun:test`` suites (``lint``).
+- ``tiers --out DIR [--tier T ...]``: collect-only test IDs per tier into ``DIR/<tier>.txt``
+  (``tiers``).
+- ``junit-args --tier T --out FILE``: the ``bun test`` arguments a tier command adds: a preload
+  that arms the tier's guards in-process and journals the run, and Bun's JUnit reporter
+  (``dialect``). ``report-check --dialect bun_test --exit-code <bun's exit code>`` then reads the
+  report; the exit code is required.
+- ``guard-evidence REPORT --tier T``: the report's journal shows the tier's guards were armed.
+- ``affected --base REF [--head REF]``: the selector and T2 files this adapter runs.
+- ``mutation-tool``: StrykerJS with its command test runner (``mutation``), T3 only.
+- ``mutation-report --out FILE [--input FILE]``: Stryker's JSON as the shared mutation report.
+- ``conformance [--case ID ...]``: the canonical cases over this adapter's fixtures.
+
+Every ``--out`` path lies outside the checkout; guardrails never writes into the repository.
+"""
+
+from __future__ import annotations
+
+import argparse
+import shlex
+import sys

+

+
